_comment: This feature is the strongest case in the repository for mutation testing, because its
central failure mode is invisible everywhere except the pixels. If a normalised box leaks
through as pixels you get a one-pixel face at the frame origin, and nothing objects:
pick_main_face returns a centre, FaceBox validates, build_face_tracks builds tracks,
build_sendcmd clamps to a valid window, ffmpeg encodes successfully, and the clip record
says `reframe`. Every clip is cropped to the frame's left edge and the only evidence is the
output. A suite of fake detectors returning pixel tuples cannot catch that - the fakes
would be right and the real backend wrong - which is why the coordinate mutations below are
checked against tests that run the real library.
Groups: the coordinate conversion, the marker vocabulary (where a swapped operand says the
opposite of the truth), backend resolution (where a label naming the wrong backend is how
font_substituted:Arial got frozen into a golden as correct), the coverage arithmetic, and
the wiring that carries any of it to the clip record.

mutations.name: return_the_box_unconverted
mutations.old: normalised = all(abs(v) <= 1.0 for v in values)
mutations.why: the central hazard: a normalised box passed through as pixels is a one-pixel face at the frame origin, and every clip is cropped to the left edge with nothing anywhere reporting a problem

mutations.name: treat_every_box_as_normalised
mutations.old: normalised = all(abs(v) <= 1.0 for v in values)
mutations.why: the same defect from the other side - scaling an already-absolute box by the frame size sends every detection far outside it, where the clamp then collapses it

mutations.name: drop_the_clamp
mutations.old:
fx0 = max(0.0, min(float(width), min(x0, x1)))
    fy0 = max(0.0, min(float(height), min(y0, y1)))
    fx1 = max(0.0, min(float(width), max(x0, x1)))
    fy1 = max(0.0, min(float(height), max(y0, y1)))
mutations.new:
fx0, fy0 = min(x0, x1), min(y0, y1)
    fx1, fy1 = max(x0, x1), max(y0, y1)
mutations.why: MediaPipe reports boxes past the frame edge for a partially visible face; unclamped they produce a crop window outside the picture

mutations.name: test_degeneracy_before_clamping
mutations.old:
if (fx1 - fx0) < 1.0 or (fy1 - fy0) < 1.0:
        return None
mutations.new:
if (max(x0, x1) - min(x0, x1)) < 1.0 or (max(y0, y1) - min(y0, y1)) < 1.0:
        return None
mutations.why: the documented order is convert, clamp, then test: measuring before the clamp admits a box lying entirely off-frame, which is non-degenerate until it is clipped

mutations.name: accept_sub_pixel_boxes
mutations.why: rounding a tenth of a pixel outward manufactures a one-pixel 'detection' out of nothing, which then anchors the crop

mutations.name: accept_non_finite_values
mutations.old: if not all(math.isfinite(v) for v in values):
mutations.why: DECLARED EQUIVALENT, and understood rather than waved through. Removing the guard changes no return value, because the clamp already neutralises non-finite input by accident: every comparison against NaN is False, so min(width, nan) returns width and max(0.0, nan) returns 0.0, collapsing the box to zero extent, which the degeneracy test then rejects. +/-inf collapses the same way. There is therefore no input on which the guard is observable, and no test can be written for it. The guard is kept anyway because that neutralisation depends on the operand order of two min/max calls -- reorder the clamp and NaN reaches an ffmpeg crop argument as the literal string 'nan'. Correctness should not rest on an accident of argument order, so the check stays and this mutation is expected to escape.

mutations.name: facebox_no_longer_readable
mutations.old: if all(hasattr(item, attr) for attr in ("x", "y", "w", "h")):
mutations.why: FaceBox carries a leading `t` so it is not a 4-tuple; without this branch every FaceBox is silently dropped and the speaker-aware path reports coverage 0.0 for footage it just tracked successfully. This was a real defect, caught by a test rather than by review.

mutations.name: swap_the_substitution_operands
mutations.old: return f"face_detector_substituted:{requested}:{resolved}"
mutations.why: the marker then says Haar was requested and MediaPipe ran - the exact opposite of the truth, in a string an operator reads to diagnose a clip, and it still looks perfectly well-formed

mutations.name: report_the_requested_backend_not_the_resolved_one
mutations.old:
haar = _haar()
        return haar, "substituted:mediapipe:haar"
mutations.why: a clip framed by Haar reporting face_detector:mediapipe is precisely how font_substituted:Arial got frozen into a golden file as correct

mutations.name: injected_borrows_a_backend_name
mutations.old:
if injected is not None:
        return injected, "injected"
mutations.new:
if injected is not None:
        return injected, "haar"
mutations.why: a test double is not evidence that a backend works; every fake in the suite would produce clip records claiming Haar ran

mutations.name: coverage_comparison_inverted
mutations.old: if coverage > 0.0 and coverage < float(settings.reframe_coverage_floor):
mutations.why: every well-framed clip is then flagged low-confidence and every badly framed one is not, which is worse than no signal because it is trusted

mutations.name: low_confidence_on_zero_coverage
mutations.old: if coverage > 0.0 and coverage < float(settings.reframe_coverage_floor):
mutations.why: zero coverage is already reported by the existing no-faces degradation, so this adds a second name for one condition - the duplicated-fact pattern this harness has caught twice before

mutations.name: coverage_counts_frames_not_hits
mutations.old: hit = sum(1 for _t, boxes in samples if boxes)
mutations.why: coverage becomes 1.0 always, so the confidence signal exists, is reported, and means nothing

mutations.name: sampling_marker_always_emitted
mutations.old: return self.effective_fps < (self.requested_fps - 0.05)
mutations.why: the marker exists to explain a REDUCED rate; emitted on every clip it is noise, and noise is what stops a marker being read

mutations.name: cap_tolerance_removed
mutations.old: return self.effective_fps < (self.requested_fps - 0.05)
mutations.why: the effective rate is a division of two measured quantities, so an uncapped clip lands a hair either side of the requested value and a bare comparison reports the cap as binding on roughly half of them

mutations.name: markers_recorded_before_the_render_succeeds
mutations.new:
return dest


def _aspect_ratio_parts(aspect: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
mutations.why: the single-speaker path stops reporting entirely, so a clip framed by a detector says nothing about which one

mutations.name: score_ignored_in_selection
mutations.old: key=lambda d: (1.0 if d.score is None else max(0.0, d.score)) * math.sqrt(d.area),
mutations.why: the largest box wins regardless of confidence, so a bookshelf captures the framing - which is the requirement's own example

mutations.name: area_dominates_confidence
mutations.old: key=lambda d: (1.0 if d.score is None else max(0.0, d.score)) * math.sqrt(d.area),
mutations.new: key=lambda d: (1.0 if d.score is None else max(0.0, d.score)) * d.area,
mutations.why: weighting by area rather than linear extent makes confidence nearly irrelevant: a 400x400 box at 0.10 beats an 80x80 face at 0.95 by more than two to one. This is the version the first implementation had, and a test caught it.

mutations.name: no_scores_branch_stops_being_largest_area
mutations.old:
else:
        best = max(items, key=lambda d: d.area)
mutations.new:
else:
        best = min(items, key=lambda d: d.area)
mutations.why: the no-scores branch is the v0.11.0 behaviour verbatim and is what makes the byte-identical default achievable; changing it moves the crop on every existing clip

mutations.name: a_raising_frame_aborts_sampling
mutations.why: one bad frame is not a broken backend, and aborting discards every frame that worked

mutations.name: the_native_graph_is_never_released
mutations.old:
cap.release()
        # Requirement 2.9: MediaPipe holds a native graph. Released here rather than by the
        # caller, and in a `finally` so it happens even when sampling raises.
        _release_detector(resolved_detector)
mutations.why: MediaPipe holds a native graph; leaked, it is finalised at interpreter shutdown after its own C shim is gone, which surfaces as a TypeError from a teardown handler long after the run reported success

mutations.name: a_wrong_sized_model_is_accepted
mutations.old:
if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size != entry.size_bytes:
            return None
mutations.why: a truncated download is a file that exists with a plausible size, and constructing against it fails deep inside the native graph at the first frame of a render rather than degrading to Haar

mutations.name: the_model_digest_is_not_checked
mutations.old:
actual = digest(path)
        if actual != entry.sha256:
mutations.why: --check then passes on any file of the right length, which is the one thing a manifest exists to rule out

mutations.name: bgr_passed_to_mediapipe_as_rgb
mutations.old: rgb = np.ascontiguousarray(frame[:, :, ::-1])
mutations.why: not a crash: the model sees a blue-skinned face, detects fewer of them, and the symptom reads as 'this footage is hard' rather than 'the channels are backwards'. Declared equivalent-risk rather than expected-caught is NOT acceptable here - the real-library test should notice.
